title: Bills, vendor controls and bank reconciliation
goal: Process bills without duplicates or fraud, and reconcile a bank account to the statement with zero unexplained difference.
concept_card: Before a bill is paid, the invoice, the approval and proof of delivery must agree. Match bank-feed items to existing bills; never add them twice. Verify any vendor bank change by calling the number already on file. A reconciliation is done only at $0.00 unexplained difference.
lesson_html:
Bill, expense or check? In QuickBooks Online a bill records money owed now and paid later. An expense or check records money already paid. If you enter a bill, pay it with Pay bills so it doesn't get counted twice.

Before any bill gets paid, three things must agree:

  1. The invoice (vendor, amount, invoice number, property)
  2. Approval from the person who owns that property or job
  3. The work or goods were actually received

Duplicate bills. Look for the same vendor and amount with invoice numbers that look alike: INV-1001 and INV1001, or the same invoice sent by email and on paper.

Vendor bank changes are the top fraud risk. If a vendor asks to change where you send money, call them at the phone number already on file, not the number in the email. A second person approves the change. The person who creates a vendor should not also release payment to that vendor.

Bank reconciliation proves the books match the bank:

Bank statement ending balance − checks not yet cleared + deposits not yet cleared = Book balance

The difference must be $0.00. If it isn't, you find the reason. You never force it to balance.

Bank feed: Match, don't Add. When a bank transaction matches a bill already entered, choose Match. Choosing Add creates the expense a second time.
rule: A reconciliation with an unexplained difference is not finished, no matter how small.

qbo_steps.title: Enter a bill
qbo_steps.html: + New → Bill. Pick the vendor, enter the invoice number, date, due date, and on each line pick the account and the customer/project. Attach the PDF.

qbo_steps.title: Pay bills
qbo_steps.html: + New → Pay bills. Select the bills and the bank account. The payment then matches the bank feed.

qbo_steps.title: Review the bank feed
qbo_steps.html: Transactions → Bank transactions (sometimes under Banking). For each line, choose Match when a bill or payment already exists.

qbo_steps.title: Reconcile
qbo_steps.html: ⚙ → Reconcile. Choose the account, enter the statement ending date and balance, tick each cleared item until the Difference is $0.00.

qbo_steps.title: Check the vendor list and audit log
qbo_steps.html: Expenses → Vendors for open balances; ⚙ → Audit log to see who changed a vendor's details and when.

qbo_steps.title: Aging report
qbo_steps.html: Reports → A/P Aging Summary shows what is owed and how late it is.

scenario.text_html: Twin Home Buyer operating account, September. Bank statement ending balance $48,250.00. Check #1045 for $3,400.00 hasn't cleared. A deposit of $1,150.00 was made September 30 and isn't on the statement. QuickBooks shows a book balance of $46,025.00. The statement also shows a $25.00 service fee.
scenario.ask: What is the adjusted bank balance (statement − uncleared checks + uncleared deposits)?
scenario.explain: $48,250 − $3,400 + $1,150 = $46,000. Books show $46,025, a $25 difference: the bank fee isn't recorded yet. Record the $25 fee, and the books become $46,000. Difference $0.00.
scenario.followup: A vendor calls to say their bank changed and asks you to confirm the old account number. What do you say?

quiz.q: A vendor emails new bank account details and asks you to pay there. What do you do?
options: Update the vendor and pay
Reply to the email to confirm
Call the vendor at the number already on file, and get a second person to approve the change
Pay half to the old account and half to the new
quiz.why: Never trust contact details in the email that asks for the change. Verify independently and require a second approver.
quiz.followup: The reconciliation is off by exactly $180 and one check for $90 appears twice in the books. What happened?

quiz.q: The bank feed shows a $4,800 payment that matches an open bill in QuickBooks. You should…
options: Add it as a new expense
Match it to the bill
Exclude it
Categorize it as Uncategorized Expense
quiz.why: Adding it would record the $4,800 cost twice. Match links the payment to the bill.

quiz.q: Your reconciliation is off by $25. What next?
options: Finish anyway; it's small
Let QuickBooks create an adjustment
Find the $25 (fee, typo, missing item) and fix the record
Change the statement balance
quiz.why: Find the cause. Forcing the adjustment hides errors and makes next month harder.

quiz.q: Which pair most likely is a duplicate?
options: Same vendor, different amounts, different months
Same vendor, same amount, invoice INV-1001 and INV1001
Different vendors, same amount
Same vendor, same property, different invoice numbers and dates
quiz.why: Same vendor, same amount and nearly identical invoice numbers is the classic duplicate.

options: The person who created the vendor and entered the bill
A named approver who didn't set up the vendor
Anyone with QuickBooks access
The AI tool
quiz.why: Separate the duties: one person sets up and enters, a different person approves and releases.

task: Reconcile one real bank account for last month. List every uncleared item with its date and amount. Difference must be $0.00. Your reviewer re-checks it against the statement.
rubric: Difference is $0.00 with no forced adjustment
Every uncleared item is listed with check number or reference
Statement PDF attached to the reconciliation
Any item older than 60 days is flagged for follow-up
